record.paper_title: On some open problems of number theory
record.original_question: For a positive integer n, let s(n) be the sum of all proper divisors of n, and set s(0) = 0. For every positive integer n, is the iterated sequence n, s(n), s(s(n)), and so on bounded?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a positive integer $n$, let $s(n) = \sum_{d \mid n,\, 1 \le d < n} d$ denote the sum of the proper divisors of $n$, and set $s(0) = 0$. For a positive integer $n$, define the aliquot sequence starting at $n$ by $a_0 = n$ and $a_{k+1} = s(a_k)$ for $k \ge 0$.

Prove or disprove: for every positive integer $n$, the sequence $(a_k)_{k \ge 0}$ is bounded.
artifact.status_search_result: This is the Catalan–Dickson conjecture (Catalan 1888, refined by Dickson 1913), asserting every aliquot sequence is bounded. The problem remains open. The smallest starting value whose behavior is unresolved is 276, which has been iterated for thousands of steps without termination or detection of a cycle. Guy and Selfridge have conjectured the opposite, that some aliquot sequences are unbounded.

status_evidence.title: Aliquot sequence - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: The conjecture of Catalan, as revised by Dickson, is that each aliquot sequence is bounded... no unbounded aliquot sequence is known, the least starter in doubt is 276.
status_evidence.claim: The Catalan–Dickson conjecture that every aliquot sequence is bounded is open; the smallest unresolved starter is 276.

status_evidence.title: Catalan-Dickson Conjecture - ProofWiki
status_evidence.snippet: Conjecture that every aliquot sequence terminates either at 0 or in a periodic cycle.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture is a long-standing open problem in number theory.

status_evidence.title: Catalan's Aliquot Sequence Conjecture - Wolfram MathWorld
status_evidence.snippet: Catalan's aliquot sequence conjecture states that every aliquot sequence eventually terminates...
status_evidence.claim: Status of the conjecture is unresolved.
